Module 02: Quality Control & Subsampling

Raw viral sequencing data from global databases contains significant sampling biases, sequence duplicates, and low-quality assemblies. Module 02 resolves these issues by implementing a two-stage quality control and spatio-temporal subsampling pipeline before phylogenetic reconstruction.

The module ensures phylogenetic trees and genetic selection analyses are computed on a high-quality, representative, and computationally tractable subset of genomes.

1. Stage 1: Quality Control & Prefiltering

The first stage runs the Snakemake rule qc_prefilter which executes scripts/qc_prefilter.py using BioPython (Cock et al. 2009). It applies three main filters:

  1. N-Content Filtering: Sequences with high rates of ambiguous bases (\(N\)) are discarded. Ambiguous bases prevent accurate alignment and mutation identification. The threshold is set via config["qc"]["max_n_content"] (default: 5.0%).
  2. Sequence Deduplication: Replicating sequences with identical nucleotide structures are identified via MD5 hashing and collapsed. This deduplication reduces downstream alignment and tree-building times by up to 60% without losing unique mutational variants.
  3. Underrepresented Subtype Filtering: Subtypes with fewer than a minimum count (default: 30 sequences) are filtered out to ensure statistical validity during genetic selection analysis.

2. Stage 2: Spatio-Temporal Subsampling (Augur Filter)

To prevent phylogenetic trees from being dominated by regions with massive sequencing capacity (creating a sampling bias), the Snakemake rule augur_filter runs scripts/m02_filter_wrapper.py. This wrapper dynamically executes augur filter (Hadfield et al. 2018) using a Focal + Contextual Subsampling strategy.

                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Prefiltered Sequences FASTA │
                    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                   │
                   ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                   ▼                               ▼
      ┌─────────────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────┐
      │   Focal Subsampling     │     │ Contextual Subsampling  │
      ├─────────────────────────┤     ├─────────────────────────┤
      │ Targets domestic area   │     │ Targets global partners │
      │ High sequence density   │     │ Representative samples  │
      │ e.g. Country: Indonesia │     │ e.g. MY, SG, AU, CN, IN │
      └────────────┬────────────┘     └────────────┬────────────┘
                   │                               │
                   └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                   ▼
                      ┌─────────────────────────┐
                      │    Combine & Deduplicate│
                      ├─────────────────────────┤
                      │ filtered_sequences.fasta│
                      └─────────────────────────┘

2.1. Focal Sampling

  • Target: The domestic region under investigation (configured via subsampling.focal.query). For this build, it selects Indonesian isolates (country == 'Indonesia').
  • Density: Retains a high density of local sequences to capture the complete picture of local transmission chains.

2.2. Contextual Sampling

  • Target: The neighboring travel corridors identified in our BPS demographic justification (Malaysia, Singapore, Australia, China, India, Japan).
  • Density: Subsamples global sequences at a lower density (e.g., grouped by country, year, and month) to serve as evolutionary context for ancestral reconstruction.

3. Configuration & Outputs (Tabset Examples)

Below are the configuration schemas and generated report files of Module 02:

  • 1. Configuration (config_influenza_a_mp.yaml)
  • 2. Output: QC Report (qc_report.json)
  • 3. Generated Command Wrapper
# [M02] Quality Control & Spatio-Temporal Filter
qc:
  max_n_content: 5.0              # Discard sequences with >5% ambiguous bases
  dedup: true                     # Remove identical duplicate sequences

subsampling:
  # Base Settings (used when focal.enabled is false)
  group_by: "subtype country year month"
  sequences_per_group: 10
  max_sequences: null
  min_length: 800
  seed: 42
  query: "country in ['Indonesia', 'Singapore', 'Malaysia', 'Thailand', 'Vietnam', 'Philippines', 'Myanmar', 'Cambodia', 'Laos', 'Brunei']"

  # Targeted Background Subsampling (Focal vs Contextual)
  focal:
    enabled: false                # Toggle to enable split focal/contextual sampling
    query: "country == 'Indonesia'"
    max_sequences: null
    sequences_per_group: 50
    group_by: "subtype year month"
    
  contextual:
    query: "country != 'Indonesia'"
    max_sequences: null
    sequences_per_group: 3
    group_by: "subtype country year month"
{
  "timestamp": "2026-06-29T14:40:00Z",
  "input_records": 50750,
  "retained_after_n_filter": 48123,
  "retained_after_deduplication": 12845,
  "retained_after_subtype_filter": 12512,
  "dropped_n_filter": 2627,
  "dropped_duplicates": 35278,
  "dropped_subtype_filter": 333
}

Depending on whether focal.enabled is true or false, the pipeline invokes Augur in one of two ways:

Option A: Base Subsampling (focal.enabled: false - Default)

# Filter sequences across Southeast Asia countries using base parameters
augur filter \
    --sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/prefiltered_sequences.fasta \
    --metadata results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m01/metadata_enriched.tsv \
    --min-length 800 \
    --subsample-seed 42 \
    --exclude-ambiguous-dates-by any \
    --query "country in ['Indonesia', 'Singapore', 'Malaysia', 'Thailand', 'Vietnam', 'Philippines', 'Myanmar', 'Cambodia', 'Laos', 'Brunei']" \
    --sequences-per-group 10 \
    --group-by subtype country year month \
    --output-sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/filtered_sequences.fasta

Option B: Focal + Contextual Subsampling (focal.enabled: true)

# 1. Filter local Indonesian isolates (Focal)
augur filter \
    --sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/prefiltered_sequences.fasta \
    --metadata results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m01/metadata_enriched.tsv \
    --min-length 800 \
    --subsample-seed 42 \
    --exclude-ambiguous-dates-by any \
    --query "country == 'Indonesia'" \
    --sequences-per-group 50 \
    --group-by subtype year month \
    --output-sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/filtered_sequences.fasta.focal.fasta

# 2. Filter global/neighboring background isolates (Contextual)
augur filter \
    --sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/prefiltered_sequences.fasta \
    --metadata results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m01/metadata_enriched.tsv \
    --min-length 800 \
    --subsample-seed 42 \
    --exclude-ambiguous-dates-by any \
    --query "country != 'Indonesia'" \
    --sequences-per-group 3 \
    --group-by subtype country year month \
    --output-sequences results/influenza-a-mp-sea/m02/filtered_sequences.fasta.ctx.fasta

# [Pipeline merges focal.fasta and ctx.fasta, removing duplicates]

3. Configuration & Parameterization

The behavior of Module 02 is governed by the quality control and spatial filtering parameters in config.yaml:

# [M02] Quality Control & Spatio-Temporal Filter
qc:
  max_n_content: 5.0              # Toleransi maksimal % base N (ambiguitas)
  dedup: true                     # Hapus sekuens duplikat identik
  min_length: 800                 # Panjang sekuens minimal (bp)
  query: "country in ['Indonesia', 'Singapore', 'Malaysia', 'Thailand', 'Vietnam', 'Philippines', 'Myanmar', 'Cambodia', 'Laos', 'Brunei']"

3.1. Parameter Tuning Dictionary

Parameter Name Allowed Values Default Value Purpose & Biological Meaning
qc.max_n_content Float 0.0 to 100.0 5.0 Sets the maximum percentage of ambiguous nucleotides (\(N\)) allowed in a sequence. Sequences exceeding 5% \(N\) are discarded. Ambiguous sequences degrade alignment quality and lead to false mismatch counts during in-silico validation.
qc.dedup true, false true When enabled, identical sequences (sharing 100% identity and same length) are collapsed into a single representative sequence. This significantly reduces downstream computational overhead for multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic building without losing epidemiological diversity.
qc.min_length Integer \(\ge 0\) 800 Excludes short or partial sequence fragments. For the Influenza MP segment (~1024 bp), setting this to 800 bp ensures that only near-full-length records are processed, preserving structural integrity for primer design.
qc.query Pandas query string SEA Countries Defines the geographic and metadata boundary of your dataset. Only sequences matching this query are retained for the subsampling pool. Changing this is how you switch between regional designs (e.g. indo-only vs sea-only).

3.2. How to Interpret the QC Report

Module 02 outputs a tabular and JSON summary (qc_report.json):

  • input_records: Total raw input sequences.
  • retained_after_n_filter: Number of sequences passing the \(N\)-content threshold. A major drop here indicates poor sequencing quality in your raw data.
  • retained_after_deduplication: Number of sequences after collapsing duplicates. For highly sampled pathogens, deduplication can shrink the database by \(>70\%\), which is normal and desirable.

4. Inputs, Outputs & Files

The files involved in Module 02 are summarized below:

File Role Path Format Description
Input Sequences results/{build}/m01/raw_sequences.fasta FASTA Raw sequences from Module 01.
Input Metadata results/{build}/m01/metadata_enriched.tsv TSV Nextclade-enriched metadata table.
QC Sequences results/{build}/m02/prefiltered_sequences.fasta FASTA Sequences post N-filtering and deduplication.
QC Report results/{build}/m02/qc_report.json JSON Summary statistics of sequence filter counts.
Final Filtered results/{build}/m02/filtered_sequences.fasta FASTA Final subsampled sequences ready for alignment.

5. Troubleshooting & Limitations

5.1. Ambiguous Date Exclusions

  • Problem: Crucial local sequences are missing in the final alignment.
  • Cause: Augur filter defaults to dropping sequences with incomplete dates (e.g. 2024-XX-XX or 2024-06-XX). If the command includes --exclude-ambiguous-dates-by any, these are excluded.
  • Solution: The pipeline’s metadata sanitizer (Module 01) resolves this by dynamically filling day or month wildcards with standard middle-points (e.g. 15 for day, 06 for month) when exact temporal precision is not mandatory for downstream selection analyses.

References

Cock, Peter J. A. et al. 2009. “Biopython: Freely Available Python Tools for Computational Molecular Biology and Bioinformatics.” Bioinformatics 25 (11): 1422–23. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163.
Hadfield, James et al. 2018. “Nextstrain: Real-Time Tracking of Pathogen Evolution.” Bioinformatics 34 (23): 4121–23. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bty407.
